kill_argument: The paper's whole claim is procedural: the outcome analysis was fixed before any outcome was read. The analysis adds nothing. Its estimate ($1,573) reproduces a known AIPW-GRF number on this sample, the failed placebo removes any causal reading, and its one decision (H1) holds by $9.6, which three of five fixed seeds, three triggering checks and a weak confounder each reverse. A procedural paper must describe its departures exactly. This version now lists the three post-results reporting changes, but it calls all three 'more cautious' and says none changes 'a decision rule'. In fact one departs from a rule the paper lists among its fixed decision rules, and another reads a failed robustness check as noise after seeing it. The paper also cites double machine learning for bias removal whose theorem needs overlap that this sample visibly fails (no lower clip; most CPS propensities below 0.01). These are wording faults, not hidden analysis choices. Tried and held: every paper-r1 fix; the JASA Table 2/3 numbers and the Biometrika abstract checked at source; nothing in runs, claim values, numbers, tables or figures changed since the clean rerun; validate --strict passes; the PDF is newer than its source.

findings.text: The deviations section omits a post-results departure from a fixed reporting rule, and the paper's central procedural claim depends on that list being complete. plan.json design.method.sensitivity fixes the reading rule: 'The paper names the strongest benchmark group to which the conclusion is robust and the weakest to which it is not.' sens-imbens logs strongest_robust_zero = 'black' and n_robust_zero = 3. After the results (results-r1 F2), the paper replaced those three 'robust' verdicts with 'no information' (main.tex Sec. 8 para. 3, Table tab:sens 'Verdict' column, Fig. fig:sens caption). The change is conservative and argued openly in Sec. 8, but Sec. 4.6 'Sensitivity reading' still describes the rule as applied, Sec. 11 (deviations and disclosures 1-7) does not list it, and the intro ('every decision rule were fixed and logged before any outcome value was read') and conclusion ('every choice that could have been tuned to the outcome was fixed and logged first') say no such change exists. The other reporting additions made at the results review are listed only as numbers computed (disclosure 2), not as changes to wording: the 'within cross-fitting noise' qualifier on H1 (results-r1 F1) and the reading of the rob-trim trigger as noise, not an overlap failure (results-r1 F3; Sec. 7). Remedy (text only, no run): add a disclosure stating that after the results, at review, (i) the sensitivity rule's literal output (conclusion robust to black, the strongest robust group; also married, nodegree) was reported as uninformative because R2_D is floored at 0 for those groups, and (ii) the H1 noise qualifier and the trim-trigger reading were added. Then qualify the intro and conclusion sentences (e.g., 'fixed first, except the reporting changes listed in Section 11').

findings.text: Three statements do not match the paper's own tables. (a) Intro line 96, 'Third, the positive sign is fragile': every robustness point estimate is positive (Sec. 7, line 626: 'Each point estimate is positive'). What is fragile is whether the interval excludes zero; only the sensitivity analysis can reverse the sign. (b) Intro lines 96-97 ('Three of the four pre-specified checks that can trigger the design's disagreement rule') and Limitations line 805 ('three of four triggering checks'): five rows can trigger. Table tab:main marks Hajek IPW 'yes^d' and Fig. fig:forest marks it 'yes*'. Sec. 7 line 661 has the accurate wording, 'through the H1 decision'. (c) Sec. 4.1 lines 291-293, 'every run that reports an ATT targets the same estimand': rob-diff74 reports an ATT on re78 - re74, which Table tab:main note e and Sec. 7 call 'a different estimand'. Remedy: change the wording in these three places.

findings.text: The main title asks whether 'Observational Estimators' (plural) can 'Recover an Experimental Job-Training Effect'. The paper runs one pre-committed estimator, refuses a causal reading because H3 failed, and treats the benchmark comparison as a description with no verdict ('a description that the failed placebo stops us from reading as success'). So the paper does not answer the title question. The title comes from the seed task, and the subtitle is accurate. Cheapest remedy: one sentence in the introduction saying that the paper does not answer the title question and why. Alternatively, lead with the subtitle.
findings.response: Writer: new introduction sentence: the paper answers the title question for one pre-specified estimator on one benchmark sample, not for observational estimators in general, and, because the placebo failed, cannot say whether even this estimator recovers the program's effect.
findings.ruling: Fixed: the new intro paragraph limits the answer to one pre-specified estimator on one sample, and says the failed placebo leaves even that unanswered.

findings.text: Disclosure 3 overstates how harmless the post-results reporting changes are, in two ways. (i) It says 'None of these changes an estimate or a decision rule', and plan.json's matching disclosure says the same. But Sec. 4.6 lists 'Sensitivity reading' among the 'Hypotheses and decision rules' ('All rules below were fixed before any outcome value was read') and now says 'This rule was not applied as written'. Change (a) is a departure from a fixed rule, a reporting rule rather than the H1/H3 rules. (ii) The intro ('three results were reported more cautiously than the fixed rules alone would have reported them'), disclosure 3 ('more cautiously than the fixed rules alone required') and the conclusion ('each of which made the report more cautious') describe all three changes as cautious. That fits (a) and (b). Change (c) reads a triggered robustness check as 'consistent with cross-fitting and refitting noise ..., not with an overlap failure'. That interpretation was added after the result was seen, and it lowers the weight a reader gives to a robustness failure, which is the opposite of caution. Part of (c) was fixed before the results: plan.json design.method.control_only_trimming already said what rob-trim measures and that the dropped men carry 0.09% of the weight. Only the 'noise' reading is post-results. I asked for this reading myself in results-r1 F3, so the fault is in how it is labelled, not in its presence. Remedy (text only, no run): say that (a) departs from the fixed sensitivity reading rule, and that none of the changes alters an estimate or the H1, H3 or disagreement rules; say that (c)'s 'refitting noise' reading is a post-results interpretation that discounts a trigger, while what the check measures was fixed in the design; drop 'each of which made the report more cautious', or limit it to (a) and (b), in the intro, disclosure 3, the conclusion and the plan.json disclosure.

findings.text: The citation added at paper-r1 says more than the source. Sec. 4.3 says the estimator 'combines an orthogonal (doubly robust) score for the ATT with cross-fitting, which removes the bias that regularization and overfitting in machine-learned nuisance functions would otherwise cause (Chernozhukov et al., 2018)'. That is unconditional. Chernozhukov et al. prove this for the ATTE score (5.4) only under Assumption 5.1 (arXiv v7 p. 37). It requires strict overlap, P(eps <= m0(X) <= 1 - eps) = 1 (5.1(c)), and an estimated propensity with ||m_hat - 1/2||_inf <= 1/2 - eps (5.1(f)), i.e. bounded away from 0 and 1, plus product-rate conditions on the nuisance errors. This study removed the lower clip (DEV-5). Fig. fig:overlap shows 'almost every CPS man has a propensity far below 0.01', and the treated group is 185 men (Kish ESS of the weighted controls is small). So the theorem's conditions are visibly not met here. The approximation is asymptotic in any case, and Limitations already says the normal approximation may under-cover. Claim c-dml-crossfit itself is accurate; the paper's sentence is the problem. Remedy (text only): write 'is designed to remove ... under regularity conditions that include strict overlap and fast enough nuisance convergence (their Assumption 5.1); with the lower clip removed and most CPS propensities below 0.01, these conditions are not met here, and the paper relies on the guarantee only as motivation'. Or drop the clause and cite the paper for the score alone.
